title: How to become a volunteer
titleCn: 如何成为志愿者：义工中心电话咨询

paragraphs.text: Part one.
You will hear a telephone conversation between a woman who works at a volunteer center and a student finding out about how he can volunteer.
First, you have some time to look at questions one to five.
Now listen carefully and answer questions one to five.
Hello, Volunteer Center.
Oh, good morning. I saw an advert about volunteering, you know, doing some unpaid work for charity, and I wanted to get some more information.
Sure. Can I take your name?
Yes, it's John Smith.
Well, hi John. My name is Karen, and I'm one of the advisors here at the Volunteer Center. What would you like to know?
Well, I've been thinking about volunteering for a while, but then I was put off as I heard that you need to give a minimum of ten hours a month. Is that right?
No, though we do say people have to give at least five hours a month. That way, both organization and volunteer benefit from the experience.
Right. Well, that'd be much more manageable, as I'm also studying full time.

Yes, many volunteers are students, and they seem to find that works for them. But can I ask, are you at university every day, as we really need people to volunteer in the week rather than over the weekend?
I was really hoping to be able to do Saturdays.
Oh, okay. Uh, just thought I'd ask. Now, what else did you want to know?
Well, there was one other thing that was worrying me.
What was that?
Well [chuckles] again, I've also heard that I would need to keep doing the job for ten weeks or more. Is that right?

Well, yes. This time your information is right. We ask for that as a minimum commitment, though many people carry on for years. It's a good amount of time for you to give it a fair go before you decided whether to continue or not.
Oh, I nearly forgot. Do I need to have my own car?
No, you don't need one. But if you have a driver's license, that's a bonus for some types of work.
Right. Well, that's good. So how do I find out what's available, and what about actually applying for a post?
We have a database here, so I can look now and see what posts come up.
Would I need to go there in person?
Not straight away. The first step is usually to fill in an application form.
Would I find that on the website?
Yes. You'll need to give your personal details and experience and so on.
What about photos?
They're not necessary, but you'll need a couple of references.
Okay. And what happens after that? Will there be an interview?
There might be, though that doesn't always happen.
So some accept you just like that?
Well, if they think you'd be good, then yes.
Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions six to ten.
Now listen and answer questions six to ten.
The search has come up with a few vacancies that should suit you if I give you the basic details.
Okay.

We have some work for volunteers who can offer domestic help. You'd be doing things like DIY, um, you know, putting up shelves and things, and you'd probably also be shopping for them, but not cooking.
And who would I be helping?
That depends, but it's often people who are sick.
Hmm, sounds interesting. Is there anything else I need to know?
Well, since these people can't get out much, they often enjoy having someone to talk to, so it helps if you're a friendly person who will chat with them.
Okay. And what about working in a charity shop? You know, where people donate stuff they don't need so the shop can sell it.
Yes, we do have a vacancy in one shop nearby.
Great. But it wouldn't be just making tea, would it?
No. You'd be doing things like arranging the displays in the windows, among other things.
Hmm. And which charity would that be for? Who would the money raised be helping?
It'd be for a charity that works to improve the lives of elderly residents in the area.
Right. I'd be happy to do that.
They also give you training on the job, so it can be really useful for people who want to work in customer service.
Oh [chuckles] well, that's a bonus.
Now, you might also be interested in volunteering to help the environment.
The environment? Hmm. Now that's something I hadn't thought of. What would I be doing?
To give you an example, it might include picking up rubbish from beauty spots in a national park.
Hmm. Sounds interesting. I like the thought of being outdoors.
Trips tend to take place over the weekend, but the bonus is accommodation is provided, even though it usually means you're sleeping in a tent.
[chuckles] Right. Well, I think I'd like some more informa-
That is the end of part one. You now have one minute to check your answers to part one.
